Aerodynamic resistance to heat transport

Source: R/metric-aerodynamics.R
ef_rah.Rd

Computes the aerodynamic resistance to heat transport \(r_{ah}\) [s m-1] between two heights \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) above the zero-plane displacement, from the friction velocity, with optional Monin-Obukhov stability corrections for heat at both heights (neutral when both are 0).

Usage

ef_rah(u_star, z1 = 0.1, z2 = 2, psi_h_z2 = 0, psi_h_z1 = 0)

Arguments

u_star

Numeric. Friction velocity \(u_*\) [m s-1] (see ef_ustar()). Must be finite and > 0.

z1, z2

Numeric. Lower and upper heights of the resistance [m]. Must be finite with 0 < z1 < z2. Defaults 0.1 m and 2 m (Waters et al., 2002, p. 30 and Eq. 41).

psi_h_z2, psi_h_z1

Numeric. Stability corrections for heat at z2 and z1 [-]. Must be finite. The default 0 is the neutral case.

Value

A numeric vector of aerodynamic resistance \(r_{ah}\) [s m-1], with the common length of the inputs and keeping their dim. Non-positive results (not reachable with the stability functions of the calibration) are returned as NA.

Details

$$r_{ah} = \frac{\ln(z_2/z_1) - \psi_h(z_2) + \psi_h(z_1)} {k\, u_*}$$ with \(k = 0.41\). In the neutral case \(r_{ah} = \ln(z_2/z_1)/(k u_*)\). This is not the FAO-56 resistance of chapter 2, Eq. 4: METRIC uses fixed heights \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) instead of the roughness length for heat, and takes the roughness into account through \(u_*\).

Missing values propagate. Infinite values and values outside the domain raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error).

Verification status: VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): Waters et al. (2002), p. 26, Eq. 26 (neutral) and p. 34, Eq. 41 (with the stability corrections at \(z_2 = 2\) m and \(z_1 = 0.1\) m, heights given on p. 30). The cross-check with Allen et al. (2007) remains desirable but is no longer blocking.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

See also

Other aerodynamics and sensible heat functions: ef_air_density(), ef_blending_wind(), ef_calibrate_h(), ef_dt_coef(), ef_h_control(), ef_sensible_heat(), ef_ts_datum(), ef_ustar(), ef_zom()

Examples

# Neutral resistance between 0.1 m and 2 m (the defaults)
ef_rah(u_star = c(0.294349, 0.225324))
#> [1] 24.82313 32.42737

# Unstable corrections at both heights
ef_rah(0.372002, z1 = 0.1, z2 = 2, psi_h_z2 = 1.719595,
       psi_h_z1 = 0.263944)
#> [1] 10.09752
